article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Hybrid
Genetics: Tea Time × Zangria
Breeder: Wizard Trees Genetics
THC Content: 25%
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Sweet candy, citrus, berry, sour fruit
Flowering Time (Indoor): 56–63 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: October
Indoor Yield: Medium to heavy
Outdoor Yield: Medium to heavy potential
Grow Difficulty: Easy to intermediate

Happy Hour takes the candy-heavy direction of modern California cannabis and gives it considerably more structure than the name might suggest. Bred by Wizard Trees from Tea Time and Zangria, this hybrid brings together two varieties already deeply rooted in Zkittlez -influenced genetics, producing weed that favors loud confectionery sweetness, oily resin, compact flower formation, and a lingering mix of fruit and funk. Wizard Trees describes the cross as combining Tea Time’s bold candy character with a distinctly Zangria-driven twist, while finished phenotypes can move between dark, highly calyxed flowers and chunkier, paler candy-dominant buds. The common thread is intensity: even before combustion, properly cured flower can fill the surrounding air with sugary aromatics touched by RS11 , Thin Mint , sour fruit, and gas.

Unlike some exotic marijuana strains bred almost entirely around aroma, Happy Hour also received practical horticultural traits from its parents. Wizard Trees lists medium-to-heavy yields, minimal stretch, strong lateral development, dense round flowers, and a relatively quick 56–63-day flowering period. The result is a cultivar capable of satisfying both flavor-focused smokers and growers who do not want to sacrifice plant structure for elite terpenes. Its name suggests easygoing social cannabis, but the approximately 25% breeder-listed THC level means this is still potent modern flower. Moderate amounts may feel upbeat and engaging before physical relaxation becomes more noticeable, while heavier consumption can shift the experience toward a slower, more immersive state.
Genetics and Lineage

Happy Hour’s direct parents are Tea Time and Zangria, both from Wizard Trees’ contemporary breeding program. Tea Time is officially listed as Zkittlez × RS11. Wizard Trees explains that the project was designed to reinforce Zkittlez’s candy characteristics while borrowing the stronger plant and flower structure of RS11. Tea Time consequently combines intense sweet-fruit terpenes with better yield potential and more substantial floral architecture than highly flavor-driven Z lines sometimes provide on their own. Wizard Trees lists Tea Time at 8–9 weeks with medium-to-heavy production, traits that carry naturally into the Happy Hour cross.

Zangria introduces another layer of Z ancestry but takes the genetic family in a different direction. The original cultivar combines Zkittlez, also known as The Original Z, with Thin Mint Cookies. That pairing brings bright candy and fruit from Z together with the denser resin, cookie character, mint, and deeper gas associated with Thin Mint genetics. Wizard Trees has used Zangria extensively as breeding material, and its influence appears throughout newer strains such as Zangbanger , Limelight, British Delight, and Happy Hour.

The genetic overlap is important because Happy Hour does not simply contain one Z-flavored parent. Both sides of the pedigree reinforce candy-oriented traits, yet RS11 and Thin Mint provide enough structure, cream, funk, and gas to prevent the resulting flower from becoming one-dimensional. Wizard Trees notes that different phenotypes can reveal the parents in visibly different ways: some lean toward Zangria with darker coloration and pronounced calyx formation, while others produce lighter, chunkier flowers that emphasize Tea Time’s candy side. This variation gives growers room to select for either deeper Zangria funk or a brighter confectionery expression while retaining the central Happy Hour identity.
Effects and Experience

Happy Hour tends to fit its name most naturally when consumed in moderate quantities. The early portion of the experience can feel buoyant and mentally brighter, with ordinary activities becoming more entertaining and social interaction flowing more easily. Creative work, music, casual conversation, gaming, or an afternoon spent outside can pair well with the initial cerebral lift. Rather than delivering the sharply electric stimulation of a classic narrow-leaf sativa, the mental change is generally smoother and more rounded, helped by the relaxing genetics carried through Zangria, RS11, and Thin Mint.

As time passes, a more noticeable physical softness can develop underneath that upbeat beginning. Muscular tension may become less prominent, the pace of thought can slow slightly, and the session gradually becomes more comfortable and less task-oriented. This makes the hybrid adaptable: a smaller serving can suit the latter part of the day without automatically ending productivity, while a larger amount may be better reserved for evenings when concentration and coordination no longer matter.

Potency should still guide consumption. Wizard Trees lists Happy Hour at approximately 25% THC, placing it well above low-potency marijuana. The actual percentage in packaged flower can change from one grow and phenotype to another, but consumers with limited tolerance should assume the cultivar can be strong. Excessive THC may produce anxiety, dizziness, impaired short-term memory, dry mouth, or uncomfortable mental fog. A sweet, smooth smoke does not indicate mild effects, so dose should be based on tolerance rather than flavor.
Medical Benefits

Happy Hour has not been studied in clinical trials as a treatment for any particular disease, and there is no evidence that the strain itself provides a uniquely predictable medical outcome. That distinction matters because commercial cannabis cultivars can vary significantly in cannabinoid concentration and terpene chemistry even when sold under the same name. Medical marijuana patients may nevertheless be attracted to its balance of mood elevation and progressive physical relaxation when seeking temporary relief from discomfort, poor appetite, stress, or difficulty settling down later in the day.

The broader research on cannabis provides some context. Reviews from the National Academies found substantial evidence that cannabis or cannabinoids can help chronic pain in adults, while more limited evidence exists for sleep and several other commonly discussed uses. These conclusions concern cannabinoids generally, however, rather than Happy Hour or any other specific cultivar. A 25% THC flower also represents a very different exposure from lower-dose oral formulations or standardized cannabinoid medications used in clinical research.

High THC can create undesirable effects alongside any perceived benefit. Anxiety, impaired concentration, altered judgment, dizziness, increased heart rate, and problems with coordination can occur, particularly after larger doses. Cannabinoids may also interact with certain prescription medicines. Medical cannabis patients using other medications or treating persistent symptoms should discuss marijuana use with an appropriate healthcare professional instead of assuming that a particular strain name predicts a therapeutic response.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Candy dominates the Wizard Trees description of Happy Hour, but there is more happening beneath the sweetness. The breeder describes loud candy terpenes layered over recognizable traces of RS11 and Thin Mint, followed by a thick, smooth smoke and a sticky-sweet flavor that continues after the exhale. The repeated Zkittlez influence from both halves of the family tree helps explain the intensity. Instead of smelling like a single fresh fruit, the buds can resemble mixed fruit candy, sweet citrus, berry syrup, or sour confectionery with creamy and slightly herbal undertones.

Phenotype selection can take the aroma in more unusual directions. Bosky Genetics obtained Happy Hour seeds directly from Wizard Trees and selected its own keeper after a full hunt. Bosky describes that plant as unmistakably Zkittlez-gas driven, with sharp sweetness supported by a deeper fuel backbone. A separate Bosky commercial expression has been characterized with clean-linen funk, cologne-like sharpness, sour candy, fermented lemon-berry notes, botanical warmth, and a solvent-like edge. These details show how widely the same genetic population can move while retaining its central sweet-and-funky personality.

The palate typically begins with the brightest candy flavors before the secondary genetics become more obvious. Sweet fruit and citrus can lead the inhale, while cream, mint, gas, or herbal spice gain strength toward the finish. Proper curing is essential. The brighter aromatic compounds responsible for candy, fruit, and citrus impressions are particularly vulnerable to heat and prolonged air exposure, so old or poorly stored flower may present far more gas and earth than a fresh jar from the same cultivar.
Growing Information

Happy Hour comes with substantially more breeder cultivation information than many modern strains. Wizard Trees lists an indoor flowering period of 56–63 days, medium-to-heavy yield potential, medium-to-tall overall height in its specification table, and suitability for indoor or outdoor cultivation. The breeder’s descriptive notes add an important detail: the plants show minimal flowering stretch and develop strong lateral branching, stacking dense, rounded buds along the stems rather than relying entirely on one dominant central cola.

That architecture offers several advantages indoors. Growers can establish a relatively even canopy during vegetative growth, then use the cultivar’s lateral branching to spread production across multiple flower sites. Light topping or low-stress training can be useful where legal, particularly before the plant enters its flowering cycle. Because stretch is limited, cultivators should establish much of the desired canopy size before changing the photoperiod rather than expecting the plant to double dramatically after flowering begins. Dense flowers also make late-cycle airflow important, especially as resin production increases.

Wizard Trees specifically emphasizes the oily, terpene-rich resin, noting that the cultivar can be appealing for hash production as well as flower. Heavy trichome production raises the importance of careful environmental control and post-harvest handling. Excess humidity around compact buds can increase mold risk, while excessive late-flower temperatures can reduce aromatic quality. Stable temperatures, consistent airflow, and avoiding unnecessary stress near harvest help protect both resin and volatile flavor compounds.

A separate commercial hunt by Bosky provides useful real-world observations. Its selected plant remained medium to short, produced strong side branches, and stacked dense flowers from the upper canopy into lower sites. Bosky specifically praised its productivity, resin coverage, structure, and consistency. Those characteristics align well with Wizard Trees’ own medium-heavy yield designation while showing why phenotype selection remains important. One keeper may stay shorter and denser while another stretches slightly more or favors darker Zangria-like flowers.

Drying should receive the same attention as flowering. Happy Hour’s appeal depends heavily on delicate candy and fruit aromatics that can disappear in an overly warm drying room. A gradual controlled dry followed by proper curing allows moisture to equalize through the flowers while preserving a broader aromatic spectrum. Growers who rush this stage may still produce potent marijuana, but much of what distinguishes Happy Hour from an ordinary high-THC hybrid can be lost.
FAQ
What strain is Happy Hour?

Wizard Trees’ Happy Hour is a hybrid cannabis strain made from Tea Time × Zangria. It combines multiple generations of Zkittlez-influenced genetics with RS11 and Thin Mint ancestry, creating a candy-heavy profile supported by gas, cream, herbal funk, and substantial resin production.
Who bred the Happy Hour strain?

Wizard Trees Genetics bred this version of Happy Hour. This distinction matters because other unrelated cannabis cultivars have also been sold under the Happy Hour name. The Wizard Trees version is specifically Tea Time crossed with Zangria.
How strong is Happy Hour?

Wizard Trees lists Happy Hour at approximately 25% THC. That places it in the high-potency category for marijuana flower, although actual test results can vary with phenotype, cultivation conditions, harvest maturity, and laboratory methodology.
What does Happy Hour taste like?

The core profile is sweet candy and fruit with citrus, sour confectionery, creamy mint, and gas underneath. Some phenotypes lean darker and funkier toward Zangria, while others emphasize Tea Time’s brighter candy character. Well-cured flower often leaves a noticeably sweet aftertaste.
How long does Happy Hour take to flower?

Wizard Trees gives an official flowering window of 56–63 days, or roughly 8–9 weeks. The breeder also describes minimal stretch, strong lateral branching, dense rounded flowers, and medium-to-heavy yield potential.
Final Thoughts on Happy Hour

Happy Hour is an unusually concentrated expression of the flavor direction Wizard Trees has helped popularize. Tea Time already pairs Zkittlez candy with the stronger plant structure and sweet sherbet characteristics of RS11; Zangria brings another dose of Z alongside Thin Mint Cookies. Crossing the two reinforces fruit and confectionery terpenes without abandoning gas, cream, mint, or the deeper cannabis funk needed to keep the flavor interesting.

Its cultivation characteristics make the genetics more compelling. Wizard Trees documents a relatively fast 56–63-day flowering window, limited stretch, strong lateral branching, dense buds, medium-heavy production, and oily resin. Those are meaningful traits for a cultivar centered so strongly on flavor because exceptionally aromatic weed can sometimes arrive with weak branches, excessive stretch, or disappointing production. Happy Hour was bred to offer more balance between the garden and the finished jar.

The experience mirrors that balance. Moderate amounts can begin upbeat, sociable, and creatively engaging before gradually relaxing the body, while larger doses make its approximately 25% THC potential much harder to ignore. For enthusiasts drawn to modern Z genetics, Happy Hour offers more than another generic candy strain. Its traceable Wizard Trees pedigree, heavy resin, phenotype diversity, compact structure, and layers of candy, fruit, Thin Mint funk, and gas give the cultivar a clear place within the breeder’s increasingly recognizable cannabis family.
